title: Railway API Token Not Working? Fix "Not Authorized" and "Project Token not found" (Oct 2026)
summary:
Disclosure: this article was drafted with the help of an AI writing assistant. The token types, headers and error messages were checked against Railway's docs and live API on 23 Oct 2026. Originally published in Stackademic on Medium.

Railway invalidated every API token and Project Token created before its October 2026 security incident. Here is how to create the right new token, test it, and fix your CLI and CI.

Last updated: 24 Oct 2026, 1:50 PM IST. Times are in IST (UTC+5:30).

Quick answer: If your Railway API token, Project Token or CLI token stopped working on or after 21 Oct 2026, it is almost certainly because Railway invalidated every token created before its security incident. Railway's status page says those tokens "remain invalidated", so the only fix is to create a new token of the right type and update every place that used the old one. Regenerating is not optional, and no setting brings an old token back.

TL;DR

  • Old tokens are dead on purpose. Railway confirmed this on 22 Oct at 10:30 PM IST (17:00 UTC), when it declared its API fully restored.
  • Pick the right type: account token (everything you can access), workspace token (one workspace) or project token (one environment in one project).
  • Account and workspace tokens use the "Authorization: Bearer" header. Project tokens use the "Project-Access-Token" header. Mixing them up causes errors.
  • For the CLI, a project token goes in RAILWAY_TOKEN, and an account or workspace token goes in RAILWAY_API_TOKEN.
  • Update GitHub Actions secrets, CI variables, scripts and local shells. Then test.

Why did my Railway API token stop working?

On 21 Oct 2026, Railway published a security disclosure. It said an unauthorized third party may have accessed encrypted environment variables and, for some of them, obtained the decrypted contents. As part of the response, Railway invalidated all API tokens.

On 22 Oct at 10:30 PM IST, Railway's status page said the API was fully restored, with an important note: "API tokens and Project Tokens created before the security incident remain invalidated, so if you use the Public API or the cli with a token, please create a new token."

So if your token is older than the incident, nothing is wrong with your code. The token itself no longer works.

If you want the full incident timeline, I covered it in Is Railway down? What the 21–22 October 2026 Railway outage means for developers.

Which Railway token do you need?

Railway's Public API docs list these token types:

  • Account token: access to all your resources and workspaces. Railway suggests it for personal scripts and local development. It is the broadest scope, so don't share it.
  • Workspace token: access to a single workspace. Railway suggests it for team CI/CD and shared automation.
  • Project token: access to a single environment in one project. Railway suggests it for deployments and service-specific automation.
  • OAuth access token: for apps that act on behalf of other Railway users through "Login with Railway".

My rule of thumb as a Laravel and Node developer: give each job the smallest token that works. A GitHub Actions job that only runs a deploy needs a project token, not your account token.

How to create a new Railway account or workspace token

  1. Sign in to Railway and open the tokens page in your account settings.
  2. Create a new token.
  3. In the workspace dropdown, choose "No workspace" for an account token, or pick one workspace for a workspace token.
  4. Copy the token straight into your password manager or CI secret store. Treat it like a password.

How to create a new Railway project token

  1. Open the project in Railway.
  2. Go to the project settings and open the tokens page.
  3. Create a token for the environment you need (for example, production).
  4. Copy it into your CI secret store.

A project token only works for the one environment it was created for. If you deploy to staging and production, you need one token per environment.

How to test your new Railway token with curl

The Railway API endpoint is https://backboard.railway.com/graphql/v2. These test queries come from Railway's docs.

Account token (returns your name and email):

curl --request POST \
  --url https://backboard.railway.com/graphql/v2 \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCOUNT_TOKEN' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"query":"query { me { name email } }"}'

Project token (returns the project and environment IDs). Note the different header:

curl --request POST \
  --url https://backboard.railway.com/graphql/v2 \
  --header 'Project-Access-Token: YOUR_PROJECT_TOKEN' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"query":"query { projectToken { projectId environmentId } }"}'

A workspace token can't run the "me" query, because that data belongs to your personal account. Railway's docs give a separate workspace query that needs your workspace ID.

What the errors look like

I sent both test queries with a deliberately invalid token on 23 Oct 2026. In both cases the API returned HTTP 200, not 401, with an error inside the JSON:

  • With a bad Bearer token, the "me" query returned the message "Not Authorized".
  • With a bad Project-Access-Token, the "projectToken" query returned the message "Project Token not found".

Both errors carried the code INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, which is how Railway's docs say authorization failures are reported. So don't rely on the HTTP status code alone. Read the errors array. If you see either message with a token you created before 21 Oct, create a new one.

How to fix Railway CLI token errors

Railway's CLI docs say:

  • Put a project token in RAILWAY_TOKEN for project-level actions, such as railway up, railway redeploy and railway logs.
  • Put an account or workspace token in RAILWAY_API_TOKEN for account-level actions.

Here is a CI-style deploy with a project token, in the form Railway's docs show:

RAILWAY_TOKEN=your-new-project-token railway up

On my machine (Railway CLI 5.71.0, 23 Oct 2026), an invalid token gave these messages:

  • With RAILWAY_TOKEN: "Unauthorized. Please check that your RAILWAY_TOKEN is valid and has access to the resource you're trying to use."
  • With RAILWAY_API_TOKEN: "Unauthorized. Please check that your RAILWAY_API_TOKEN is valid and has access to the resource you're trying to use."
  • With no token and no login: "Unauthorized. Please login with railway login"

If you work interactively on your own laptop, you don't need a token at all. Run railway login, or railway login --browserless on a remote server, then run railway whoami to confirm.

How to update GitHub Actions and other CI secrets

  1. In GitHub, open the repository, then Settings, then Secrets and variables, then Actions.
  2. Edit the existing secret (for example RAILWAY_TOKEN or RAILWAY_API_TOKEN) and paste the new value. Keep the same name so your workflow file doesn't need to change.
  3. Re-run the last failed workflow.

Railway's own PR-environment example reads RAILWAY_API_TOKEN from a GitHub secret. Its docs add a note: if you use a workspace project, make sure the token is scoped to your account, not a specific workspace. Do the same in GitLab CI, Bitbucket, Jenkins or any cron server that calls Railway.

Also check these places, which people often forget:

  • A .env file on your laptop or a teammate's laptop.
  • Shell profiles such as .bashrc or .zshrc that export RAILWAY_TOKEN.
  • Scripts that call the GraphQL API from another server.
  • Third-party dashboards or bots that you gave a Railway token.

Common mistakes that look like a broken token

  • Using Bearer with a project token. Project tokens need the Project-Access-Token header.
  • Running "me" with a workspace or project token. That query only works with an account token.
  • Using a project token for the wrong environment. It only works for the environment it was created for.
  • Hitting the rate limit. Railway's docs list 100 requests per hour on Free, 1,000 on Hobby and 10,000 on Pro, plus 10 requests per second on Hobby and 50 on Pro. Over the limit you get HTTP 429. Wait for the Retry-After interval.
  • Swapping the CLI variables. A project token in RAILWAY_API_TOKEN, or an account token in RAILWAY_TOKEN, fails.

Token hygiene after the incident

  • One token per job, with the smallest scope that works.
  • Store tokens only in a secret manager or CI secrets, never in Git.
  • Don't paste tokens into chats, tickets or screenshots.
  • The Railway CLI itself warns that railway run env and railway run printenv can print secret values. Don't share that output.
  • Delete tokens you no longer use.

New tokens fix access, but they don't fix leaked app secrets. Railway still recommends rotating every environment variable you stored there. Its engineering blog has step-by-step guides for databases, GitHub, AWS, GCP, Stripe and AI provider keys.

FAQ

Why is my Railway API token not working?
Railway invalidated all API tokens and Project Tokens created before its October 2026 security incident. Create a new token and replace the old one everywhere.

Why do I get "Project Token not found" on Railway?
The project token is invalid, deleted, or older than the incident. It also happens if you send a project token through the wrong header. Create a new project token and send it in the Project-Access-Token header.

How do I get a Railway API token?
Account and workspace tokens are created on the tokens page in your account settings (railway.com/account/tokens). Project tokens are created on the tokens page in your project settings.

What's the difference between RAILWAY_TOKEN and RAILWAY_API_TOKEN?
RAILWAY_TOKEN holds a project token for project-level actions such as deploys. RAILWAY_API_TOKEN holds an account or workspace token for account-level actions.

Will my old Railway tokens start working again?
Railway says pre-incident API tokens and Project Tokens remain invalidated. Plan on replacing them, not waiting.

Do I need a token to use the Railway CLI on my laptop?
No. Run railway login for an interactive session. Railway revoked CLI sessions during the incident, so if the CLI says you're not authorized, run railway logout and then railway login (Railway guide). Tokens are for CI and automation.

Is the Railway API back up?
Railway said the API was fully restored on 22 Oct 2026 at 10:30 PM IST. Railway published its preliminary incident report at 10:08 PM IST on 23 Oct and marked the incident resolved at 3:36 AM IST on 24 Oct, but new signups are still paused. Old API tokens and Project Tokens remain invalid. Check status.railway.com for the current state.

Related reading

  • Is Railway down? What the 21–22 October 2026 Railway outage means for developers
  • How to export or back up your Railway database (Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis) before you migrate
  • Railway alternatives in 2026: Render, Fly.io, AWS or Coolify? A fair migration guide
  • Is Railway safe now? What the October 2026 breach means, plus a hosting security checklist

Sources: Railway status page, Railway security disclosure, Railway Public API docs, Railway CLI docs, Railway CLI deploying docs. All checked on 23 Oct 2026.

title: AZ-104 exam guide 2026: format, skills measured, renewal and how to prepare
summary:
Exam AZ-104, Microsoft Azure Administrator, earns the Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate certification. This guide covers who it is for, how the exam works, what the five skill areas test, what changed in the April 2026 update, how to renew and a suggested way to prepare.

AZ-104 at a glance

Detail AZ-104
Awarded by Microsoft
Certification Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate
Level Intermediate (associate)
Time 100 minutes
Questions Not listed for AZ-104; Microsoft says most of its exams have 40–60
Passing score 700 on a scale of 1 to 1,000 (scaled)
Delivery Proctored, scheduled through Pearson VUE
Languages English, Chinese (Simplified), Korean, Japanese, French, Spanish, German, Portuguese (Brazil), Chinese (Traditional), Italian
Price Depends on the country or region where you take it
Renewal Every 12 months, free, with an online assessment on Microsoft Learn

Who it is for

Microsoft describes the candidate as someone with subject matter expertise in implementing, managing and monitoring an organization’s Microsoft Azure environment, including virtual networks, storage, compute, identity, security and governance.

An Azure administrator often works as part of a larger team that implements an organization’s cloud infrastructure. You also coordinate with other roles to deliver Azure networking, security, database, application development and DevOps solutions.

Recommended experience

Microsoft says you should be familiar with:

  • operating systems
  • networking
  • servers
  • virtualization

You should also have experience with PowerShell, Azure CLI, the Azure portal, Azure Resource Manager templates or Bicep files and Microsoft Entra ID. The certification page and study guide do not list any formal prerequisite.

The exam format

You have 100 minutes. The exam is proctored and may include interactive components. Microsoft does not reveal question types in advance, but its exam sandbox lets you try the exam interface and question formats before you book. Most questions cover features that are generally available, though commonly used Preview features can appear.

  • Scoring: you need 700 or more on a scale of 1 to 1,000. This is a scaled score, so it may not equal 70% of the points. There is no penalty for guessing, and some questions may be unscored without telling you which.
  • Microsoft Learn is open: on associate and expert exams you can open Microsoft Learn in a split screen. No extra time is added and the clock keeps running.
  • Breaks: five minutes are built into the exam time for breaks. The clock keeps running, and you cannot return to questions you saw before the break.
  • Language: if the exam is not available in your preferred language, you can request an extra 30 minutes.
  • Retakes: you must wait 24 hours after a first failed attempt and 14 days between later attempts. You cannot take the same exam more than five times in 12 months from your first attempt.

The official skills measured

The AZ-104 study guide groups the exam into five skill areas. This is how it describes them, in brief:

Skill area Weight What it covers
Manage Azure identities and governance 20–25% Creating and managing Microsoft Entra users and groups, licenses, external users and self-service password reset. Built-in Azure roles, role assignments at different scopes and interpreting access. Azure Policy, resource locks, tags, resource groups, subscriptions, management groups, and managing costs with alerts, budgets and Azure Advisor.
Implement and manage storage 15–20% Storage firewalls and virtual networks, SAS tokens, stored access policies, access keys and identity-based access for Azure Files. Creating storage accounts, redundancy, object replication, encryption, Storage Explorer and AzCopy. File shares, blob containers, storage tiers, soft delete and snapshots, lifecycle management and blob versioning.
Deploy and manage Azure compute resources 20–25% Reading, changing and deploying ARM templates and Bicep files, and exporting or converting them. Creating VMs, encryption at host, moving VMs, sizes, disks, availability zones and sets, and Virtual Machine Scale Sets. Azure Container Registry, Container Instances and Container Apps. App Service plans, scaling, certificates and TLS, custom DNS names, backup, networking and deployment slots.
Implement and manage virtual networking 15–20% Virtual networks, subnets, peering, public IP addresses, user-defined routes and troubleshooting connectivity. Network security groups and application security groups, effective security rules, Azure Bastion, and service and private endpoints. Azure DNS, and configuring and troubleshooting internal or public load balancers.
Monitor and maintain Azure resources 10–15% Metrics, log settings and log queries in Azure Monitor, alert rules, action groups and alert processing rules, Azure Monitor Insights, Network Watcher and Connection monitor. Recovery Services and Backup vaults, backup policies, backup and restore, Azure Site Recovery, failover to a secondary region, and backup reports and alerts.

Identities and governance and compute carry the most weight. Monitoring and maintenance is the smallest area, but it is still up to 15% of the exam.

What changed in 2026

Skills measured as of April 17, 2026. Microsoft’s change log marks the audience profile and five groups as minor changes: Configure Azure Files and Azure Blob Storage, Create and configure virtual machines, Provision and manage containers in the Azure portal, Configure and manage virtual networks in Azure, and Monitor resources in Azure. The skill areas listed in the change log are marked as no change.

Microsoft updates the English version of an exam first. Localized versions are updated about eight weeks after the English version, although Microsoft says this schedule can slip.

Official study resources

  • the AZ-104 study guide, which lists every skill measured and the change log
  • self-paced learning paths and modules, or an instructor-led course, linked from the study guide
  • the Azure documentation, including Microsoft Entra ID, Azure Policy, Azure Storage, ARM templates, Container Instances, Container Apps, App Service, Azure DNS, Azure Bastion, Azure Monitor, Network Watcher, Site Recovery and Azure Backup
  • the free Practice Assessment on Microsoft Learn, which shows the style, wording and difficulty of exam questions
  • the exam sandbox, to practise the exam interface
  • the Exam AZ-104 prep videos and the Exam Readiness Zone

A suggested 6-week study plan

This is our suggested plan. It follows the five skill areas and gives time in line with their weights.

  1. Week 1: Identity and governance. Entra users and groups, licenses, external users and SSPR, then Azure RBAC roles and scopes, Azure Policy, locks, tags, management groups and cost controls.
  2. Week 2: Storage. Storage accounts and redundancy, firewalls, SAS tokens and access keys, encryption, Azure Files, blob tiers, soft delete, versioning, lifecycle rules, object replication and AzCopy.
  3. Week 3: Compute. ARM templates and Bicep, VM sizes, disks, availability zones and sets, scale sets, moving VMs, containers, and App Service plans, slots, certificates and networking.
  4. Week 4: Networking. VNets and subnets, peering, user-defined routes, NSGs and application security groups, Bastion, service and private endpoints, Azure DNS and load balancers.
  5. Week 5: Monitoring and backup. Azure Monitor metrics, logs and alerts, Network Watcher, Recovery Services and Backup vaults, backup policies, restores and Site Recovery failover.
  6. Week 6: Practice and review. Take the free Practice Assessment and full-length timed practice exams, read every explanation, and revisit the areas where you score lowest. Practise finding answers quickly on Microsoft Learn, since it is open during the exam but the clock keeps running.

Keeping your certification

The Azure Administrator Associate certification has a 12-month renewal frequency. Renewal is free: you pass a short online renewal assessment on Microsoft Learn, which becomes available six months before your certification expires. event_model_payload.headline: AZ-104 exam guide 2026: format, skills measured, renewal and how to prepare
event_model_payload.summary:
Exam AZ-104, Microsoft Azure Administrator, earns the Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate certification. This guide covers who it is for, how the exam works, what the five skill areas test, what changed in the April 2026 update, how to renew and a suggested way to prepare.

AZ-104 at a glance

Detail AZ-104
Awarded by Microsoft
Certification Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate
Level Intermediate (associate)
Time 100 minutes
Questions Not listed for AZ-104; Microsoft says most of its exams have 40–60
Passing score 700 on a scale of 1 to 1,000 (scaled)
Delivery Proctored, scheduled through Pearson VUE
Languages English, Chinese (Simplified), Korean, Japanese, French, Spanish, German, Portuguese (Brazil), Chinese (Traditional), Italian
Price Depends on the country or region where you take it
Renewal Every 12 months, free, with an online assessment on Microsoft Learn

Who it is for

Microsoft describes the candidate as someone with subject matter expertise in implementing, managing and monitoring an organization’s Microsoft Azure environment, including virtual networks, storage, compute, identity, security and governance.

An Azure administrator often works as part of a larger team that implements an organization’s cloud infrastructure. You also coordinate with other roles to deliver Azure networking, security, database, application development and DevOps solutions.

Recommended experience

Microsoft says you should be familiar with:

  • operating systems
  • networking
  • servers
  • virtualization

You should also have experience with PowerShell, Azure CLI, the Azure portal, Azure Resource Manager templates or Bicep files and Microsoft Entra ID. The certification page and study guide do not list any formal prerequisite.

The exam format

You have 100 minutes. The exam is proctored and may include interactive components. Microsoft does not reveal question types in advance, but its exam sandbox lets you try the exam interface and question formats before you book. Most questions cover features that are generally available, though commonly used Preview features can appear.

  • Scoring: you need 700 or more on a scale of 1 to 1,000. This is a scaled score, so it may not equal 70% of the points. There is no penalty for guessing, and some questions may be unscored without telling you which.
  • Microsoft Learn is open: on associate and expert exams you can open Microsoft Learn in a split screen. No extra time is added and the clock keeps running.
  • Breaks: five minutes are built into the exam time for breaks. The clock keeps running, and you cannot return to questions you saw before the break.
  • Language: if the exam is not available in your preferred language, you can request an extra 30 minutes.
  • Retakes: you must wait 24 hours after a first failed attempt and 14 days between later attempts. You cannot take the same exam more than five times in 12 months from your first attempt.

The official skills measured

The AZ-104 study guide groups the exam into five skill areas. This is how it describes them, in brief:

Skill area Weight What it covers
Manage Azure identities and governance 20–25% Creating and managing Microsoft Entra users and groups, licenses, external users and self-service password reset. Built-in Azure roles, role assignments at different scopes and interpreting access. Azure Policy, resource locks, tags, resource groups, subscriptions, management groups, and managing costs with alerts, budgets and Azure Advisor.
Implement and manage storage 15–20% Storage firewalls and virtual networks, SAS tokens, stored access policies, access keys and identity-based access for Azure Files. Creating storage accounts, redundancy, object replication, encryption, Storage Explorer and AzCopy. File shares, blob containers, storage tiers, soft delete and snapshots, lifecycle management and blob versioning.
Deploy and manage Azure compute resources 20–25% Reading, changing and deploying ARM templates and Bicep files, and exporting or converting them. Creating VMs, encryption at host, moving VMs, sizes, disks, availability zones and sets, and Virtual Machine Scale Sets. Azure Container Registry, Container Instances and Container Apps. App Service plans, scaling, certificates and TLS, custom DNS names, backup, networking and deployment slots.
Implement and manage virtual networking 15–20% Virtual networks, subnets, peering, public IP addresses, user-defined routes and troubleshooting connectivity. Network security groups and application security groups, effective security rules, Azure Bastion, and service and private endpoints. Azure DNS, and configuring and troubleshooting internal or public load balancers.
Monitor and maintain Azure resources 10–15% Metrics, log settings and log queries in Azure Monitor, alert rules, action groups and alert processing rules, Azure Monitor Insights, Network Watcher and Connection monitor. Recovery Services and Backup vaults, backup policies, backup and restore, Azure Site Recovery, failover to a secondary region, and backup reports and alerts.

Identities and governance and compute carry the most weight. Monitoring and maintenance is the smallest area, but it is still up to 15% of the exam.

What changed in 2026

Skills measured as of April 17, 2026. Microsoft’s change log marks the audience profile and five groups as minor changes: Configure Azure Files and Azure Blob Storage, Create and configure virtual machines, Provision and manage containers in the Azure portal, Configure and manage virtual networks in Azure, and Monitor resources in Azure. The skill areas listed in the change log are marked as no change.

Microsoft updates the English version of an exam first. Localized versions are updated about eight weeks after the English version, although Microsoft says this schedule can slip.

Official study resources

  • the AZ-104 study guide, which lists every skill measured and the change log
  • self-paced learning paths and modules, or an instructor-led course, linked from the study guide
  • the Azure documentation, including Microsoft Entra ID, Azure Policy, Azure Storage, ARM templates, Container Instances, Container Apps, App Service, Azure DNS, Azure Bastion, Azure Monitor, Network Watcher, Site Recovery and Azure Backup
  • the free Practice Assessment on Microsoft Learn, which shows the style, wording and difficulty of exam questions
  • the exam sandbox, to practise the exam interface
  • the Exam AZ-104 prep videos and the Exam Readiness Zone

A suggested 6-week study plan

This is our suggested plan. It follows the five skill areas and gives time in line with their weights.

  1. Week 1: Identity and governance. Entra users and groups, licenses, external users and SSPR, then Azure RBAC roles and scopes, Azure Policy, locks, tags, management groups and cost controls.
  2. Week 2: Storage. Storage accounts and redundancy, firewalls, SAS tokens and access keys, encryption, Azure Files, blob tiers, soft delete, versioning, lifecycle rules, object replication and AzCopy.
  3. Week 3: Compute. ARM templates and Bicep, VM sizes, disks, availability zones and sets, scale sets, moving VMs, containers, and App Service plans, slots, certificates and networking.
  4. Week 4: Networking. VNets and subnets, peering, user-defined routes, NSGs and application security groups, Bastion, service and private endpoints, Azure DNS and load balancers.
  5. Week 5: Monitoring and backup. Azure Monitor metrics, logs and alerts, Network Watcher, Recovery Services and Backup vaults, backup policies, restores and Site Recovery failover.
  6. Week 6: Practice and review. Take the free Practice Assessment and full-length timed practice exams, read every explanation, and revisit the areas where you score lowest. Practise finding answers quickly on Microsoft Learn, since it is open during the exam but the clock keeps running.

Keeping your certification

The Azure Administrator Associate certification has a 12-month renewal frequency. Renewal is free: you pass a short online renewal assessment on Microsoft Learn, which becomes available six months before your certification expires. The assessment is unproctored and open book, takes about 45 minutes, and can be retaken as often as needed before expiry. Passing it extends your certification by one year from the expiration date. If the certification expires, you must pass the exam again.
